Logo

The cursor sits on the i.

The wordmark is lowercase saneee.in, with a pointer arrow in place of the dot on the i. That arrow is the whole idea: a studio that builds for screens. Use the supplied SVG. Never retype it in a font.

Do

  • Use the SVG files from public/img.
  • Black logo on light grounds, white on dark.
  • Keep the arrow and the i together, at the drawn size.
  • Use the S mark below about 120px wide.

Don't

  • Stretch, skew or letter-space the artwork.
  • Add shadows, glows, outlines or gradients.
  • Recolour single letters, or use colours outside the palette.
  • Set it on grey, photos or anything low contrast.

In motion

  • Logo revealThe cursor arrow lands last. 2–3 seconds, loops cleanly. For intros, reels and end cards, on ink only.
  • Hero morphOn the site, the word SANEEE folds into the sigil as you scroll.
  • Portal blobThe cursor tears a hole into the other world, and steps aside over text.
  • Easingcubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1): a fast start and a soft landing, 0.3–0.6s.

Colour

Four colours. Lime is the loud one.

Ink and paper carry almost everything. Lime marks the moments that matter: the cursor, the selection, the footer, the insane world. Grey is for supporting text only.

18.5:1Ink on paper · AAA
16.9:1Ink on lime · AAA
5.9:1Grey on paper · AA

WCAG contrast ratios. Grey passes AA for body text on paper (5.9:1) and on lime (5.4:1), so it stays fine for captions. Never put lime text on paper: it disappears.

Team accents

Each of us has a colour.

Lime belongs to the studio, and to Param. Teesha, Hardik and Smit each have their own accent, and it takes lime's place on anything they sign. Pick one here or in the nav, and the whole kit switches to it.

Where they go: a member's own posts and reels, their profile and team cards, decks and proposals they present, and their email signature. Where they don't: the logo files, the website's two worlds and studio-wide campaigns, which stay lime. Same rules as lime: ink text on top, one accent per piece, and never as text on paper. Grey fails on pink and orange, so use ink at 72% for small text there.

Two worlds

Sanely built. Insanely good.

The site has two sides with the same content. Sane is the calm, paper version. Insane is the lime version, louder and more playful. A pill switch in the nav flips between them, and the cursor's portal blob tears through from one to the other.

Typography

One custom face, one serif.

Saneee Brand leads: logo shapes, headlines, nav, buttons and labels. The italic serif adds contrast in short editorial lines. Make variety with size, line breaks and space, not more fonts.

Details

Small things people notice.

The lime cursor

The logo's arrow, used as the site's mouse pointer. Lime fill, ink outline.

Select this text

Selection

Highlighted text goes lime with ink letters. On the lime world it flips to ink with lime letters.

Grain

A fine noise over lime surfaces, like the menu bubble and the portal hole. It keeps flat lime from looking digital.

Go insane

Pills

Buttons are full pills: 1.5px outline, 44px tall, brand face. Filled in ink for the main action.

05 / Contact

Section labels

Number and name, in caps with +0.08em tracking. The number is the real order of the page.

4px

Corners

Images and panels stay almost square, at 4px. Only buttons are round.
